question: how much of mTRF's accuracy survives when its segment margin is computed only at the proposed system's 16 anchor times instead of on all reconstructable samples?

anchors.mapping: 64 Hz sample j = a // 2: the ext_common pairwise-mean sample whose 128 Hz pair {2j, 2j+1} contains a (centre 3.9 ms before a)
anchors.targets: the decoder's 64 Hz prediction and the 64 Hz pairwise-mean attended / ignored envelopes at j (its own training target), not the 128 Hz envelope sample at a

primary.decoder: mTRF-ctx units (context_matched/mtrf), stored decoder.npz, no re-fit
primary.margin: r(pred, att) - r(pred, ign) over the 16 samples j of each 5 s segment
primary.integration: ext_context.score_units = ext_common.integrate_unit (aln42.external_eval.integrate, 5 / 10 / 20 s, tau refitted on training-side windows by the unchanged rule) + ext_common.summarize; 20 s primary

secondary.decoder: Table 2 mTRF units (external_decoders/mtrf), stored decoder.npz, no re-fit
secondary.location: inside the output file, key secondary_mtrf_main_anchor16

reproduction_gate: full-window margins recomputed from the stored weights == stored margins (max abs diff <= 1e-09) on every scored segment of every unit, both decoders; engineering check, not an outcome gate

pre_stated_reading.large_drop: a large drop of mTRF toward the proposed system's level means sparse 4 Hz (16-point) scoring explains much of the gap
pre_stated_reading.small_drop: a small drop means it does not
pre_stated_reading.descriptive_quantity: per cohort / group at 20 s: share of the mTRF-ctx minus TCS accuracy gap removed by 16-anchor scoring = (mtrf_ctx - mtrf_ctx_anchor16) / (mtrf_ctx - TCS); reported, no threshold
pre_stated_reading.caveat: the proposed system still differs in features, readout training data (ss) and 128 Hz anchor targets; this isolates only the number / rate of scored points
